title: Belvedere: Masterpieces
subtitle: Embraces, portraits and still lifes reveal how closely a figure can belong to its setting—or resist it.
introduction:
Schiele's embracing bodies press into a creased sheet whose folds are scarcely calmer than their limbs. Klimt's lovers, by contrast, nearly disappear into the joined decoration of their clothes. In both pictures contact is central, but the surrounding surface makes that contact feel and look different.

The comparison extends beyond couples. A fan can balance a portrait's elaborate dress; a doorway can separate a woman from the room behind her; a slaughtered animal can disturb an otherwise recognisable still life. This selection considers how figures and objects occupy their painted ground. The familiar works reward attention alongside quieter pictures, where the same problem may be easier to isolate.
visitNote: The guide describes works in the Belvedere collection, rather than a guaranteed display list. The museum currently notes that Judith is not on view. Check the Upper Belvedere’s current collection information for loans and room changes before your visit.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s short book argues that colour and form can carry meaning beyond the objects they describe. It offers a contemporary point of comparison for Klimt, Gerstl and Schiele, whose methods differ considerably.

works.title: The Embrace
works.credit: Egon Schiele. The embrace. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The sheet does not soften the intertwined bodies into an easy resting shape. Its creases repeat and extend their angular contours, carrying the pressure of contact beyond the skin. Schiele encloses the couple within a compact arrangement against the yellow surroundings. The embrace is made visible as a relationship of bent limbs, weight and shared surface.

works.title: On the Balcony
works.credit: On the Balcony. WikiArt; WikiArt. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; complete source frame.
works.description: The woman's back keeps her attention outside while the viewer remains within the room. Her pale blue dress occupies a narrow doorway between those positions. Roofs and street are available beyond the railing, but the confined opening matters as much as the prospect. Romako makes looking out a particular bodily situation rather than simply another landscape view.

works.title: At the Wolfgangsee
works.credit: Anton Romako. At the Wolfgangsee. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/anton-romako/evening-in-the-prossau-near-gastein-1877
works.description: Low boats and a tall wayside cross establish different directions near the water. Their practical and devotional functions share a foreground before the mountains. Romako does not need to isolate the religious marker in order to give it a presence. Its vertical form distinguishes it within a lakeside environment also organised around transport and shelter.

works.title: Babette Tapecierer
works.credit: Anton Romako. Babette Tapecierer. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/anton-romako/babette-tapecierer-1876
works.description: The open fan supplies a broad pale shape below the busy neckline. Lace, bow and blue clothing frame the face against warm red, giving Romako several kinds of surface to balance. The sitter remains directly identifiable within that elaboration. Following the fan back toward the face makes the portrait's organisation clearer than treating the costume as detachable ornament.

works.title: Judith
works.medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
works.credit: Gustav Klimt. Judith and the Head of Holofernes. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/gustav-klimt/judith-and-holopherne-1901
works.description: Holofernes's severed head is partly withheld at the lower edge. Jewellery, skin and gold take visual precedence, so recognising the biblical aftermath can lag behind noticing the portrait-like figure. Klimt makes that imbalance consequential. Judith's presentation occupies most of the image, while the evidence of her violent action enters through a margin rather than through a fully staged narrative.

works.title: Forest Clearing with Thistles
works.credit: Anton Romako. Forest clearing with thistles. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/anton-romako/forest-clearing-with-thistles-1885
works.description: Thistles claim the near space that a landscape might reserve for a figure or path. Branches and overlapping growth provide depth without an easy route inward. Small openings of light do not fully clear the density. Romako gives a plant that might be passed over in a broader prospect enough prominence to organise the view.

works.title: The Kiss
works.medium: Gold, silver and platinum leaf; resin-oil colours on primed canvas; composition gold (brass), glazes and metal-leaf flakes in background
works.credit: Gustav Klimt. The Kiss (Lovers). Image credit: Joseolgon; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Interior_of_Belvedere_Palace_(8).jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Pattern nearly joins the garments into one enclosure, while exposed hands and faces preserve the particular actions of the two bodies. Bare feet and the flowered bank locate their contact at the lower edge. Klimt moves between bodily recognition and ornament. The embrace remains legible because a few unpatterned areas carry more descriptive weight than the expansive gold around them.

works.title: Girl Picking Apples
works.credit: Girl Picking Apples. WikiArt; WikiArt. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; complete source frame.
works.description: The upward reach is determined by the tree rather than by a formal portrait pose. A held branch and the extended arms connect the girl's body directly to the surrounding apples and leaves. Romako lets a small task generate the composition. The figure's relationship to the setting is practical before it becomes decorative.

works.title: Still Life with a Slaughtered Lamb
works.catalogueTitle: Still life with a slaughtered lamb
works.credit: Oskar Kokoschka. Still life with a slaughtered lamb. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/oskar-kokoschka/still-life-with-a-slaughtered-lamb
works.description: Flowers and a vessel belong to a familiar tabletop arrangement; the dead lamb changes its register. Kokoschka does not isolate the body from the other objects, and uneven marks keep the entire surface disturbed. The painting asks the still life's descriptive attention to accommodate something difficult. Material presence does not become neutral simply because its subject is motionless.

works.title: Adam and Eve
works.credit: Gustav Klimt. Adam and Eve. Image credit: Gustav Klimt; Originally from it.wikipedia ; description page is/was here . Original uploader was Melancholyblues. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Adam_and_Eve_Gustav_Klimt.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The pale standing woman takes most of the available visibility, with the darker man partly behind. Pattern gathers below their bodies instead of surrounding them equally. Klimt distributes exposure unevenly within the pair. Compared with the merged garments of *The Kiss*, this arrangement separates the figures more strongly through their different relations to light and surface.

works.title: Portrait of a Woman
works.credit: Carola Nahowska · Belvedere · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
works.description: The high pale collar lifts the profile clear of the darker room. A picture on the wall introduces another represented figure nearby, placing the sitter within an environment already containing images. Nahowska's close framing preserves only part of that interior. The portrait feels located among things rather than given an empty ground solely for its likeness.

works.title: Early Spring in the Vienna Woods
works.catalogueTitle: Early Spring in the Vienna Woods
works.credit: Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller. Early Spring in the Vienna Woods. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Bare branches remain above patches of new green, allowing the season to appear as a mixture of conditions. Children gather on a woodland slope whose close, steep terrain gives their activity a particular footing. Waldmüller links spring to this uneven piece of ground. The familiar subject gains specificity from where bodies must stand and move.

works.title: Madame Legois
works.credit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot. Madame Legois. Image credit: Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Corot_Madame_Legois.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Red above a white skirt creates a compact division of the seated figure. Joined resting hands and an upright posture remain clear against the muted setting. Corot limits the number of strong shapes, giving each a substantial role in the likeness. The encounter depends on a held bodily arrangement rather than an abundance of personal accessories.

works.title: Napoleon at the Great Saint Bernard Pass
works.catalogueTitle: Napoleon at the Great St. Bernard Pass
works.credit: Jacques-Louis David. Napoleon at the Great St. Bernard Pass. Image credit: Jacques-Louis David; Own work David Monniaux. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Napoleon_by_David_DSC03022.JPG. CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Horse, cloak, pointing arm and steep ground carry movement along related diagonals. David makes the landscape collaborate in a public image of command. The rearing animal supplies force that the rider appears able to direct. This is an organised representation of authority; treating it as an incidental record of crossing a pass would miss its central construction.

works.title: Self-Portrait, Laughing
works.credit: Richard Gerstl. Self-Portrait, Laughing. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Bright teeth and an open mouth interrupt the face's roughly worked colour. The surrounding paint continues that activity rather than providing a quiet border around the expression. Gerstl replaces the composed presentation expected of a formal self-portrait with something less settled. The picture shows a deliberately visible expression without giving certain access to the painter's underlying state of mind.

works.title: Sonja Knips
works.credit: Gustav Klimt. Sonja Knips. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The dress spreads widely, but the upper body holds a poised position near the chair's edge. A small red book interrupts the pale pink fabric. Klimt balances expansiveness with a few concentrated signs of attention, keeping the sitter from being absorbed by the costume. The forward placement gives the soft surrounding forms a more alert centre.

works.title: Still Life with Chrysanthemums and Amaryllis
works.catalogueTitle: Still Life with Chrysanthemums and Amaryllis
works.credit: Lovis Corinth. Still Life with Chrysanthemums and Amaryllis. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Petals remain recognisable while streaks of colour pass into the surrounding surface. Corinth lets a crowded bouquet become an accumulation of marks as well as a group of flowers. The two readings support one another: floral density gives the handling a subject, and the handling prevents that subject from becoming a neat inventory of separate blooms.

works.title: Still Life with Five Bottles
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. Still Life with Five Bottles. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Restricted greens and browns make variations in height and silhouette especially useful. Upright bottles stand close while a horizontal vessel interrupts their bases. Van Gogh's small group asks attention to measured differences of reflection and shape. With no narrative event to organise the scene, the placement of one container against another carries the picture.

works.title: The Chef, Le Père Paul
works.credit: Claude Monet. The Chef (Le Père Paul). Image credit: Kadı; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Claude_Monet%27s_painting.jpg. CC0 (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The white cap identifies an occupation while the close framing directs attention toward the bearded face. Monet keeps the setting subdued enough for both to remain clear. Work clothes are neither removed for ceremony nor allowed to replace the individual likeness. The portrait gives a working person a concentrated presence without surrounding him with a scene of labour.

works.title: Squatting Couple, The Family
works.credit: The Family. WikiArt; Egon Schiele. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The crouching man, seated woman and low child build a triangular group through position. Their bodies touch the same compact field without sharing one repeated gesture. Schiele makes the family a visible arrangement among separate people. The title should not be allowed to turn that construction automatically into a documentary account of a particular domestic moment.

closingSections.title: Compare the surroundings of an embrace
paragraphs: Return to Schiele's creased sheet and Klimt's patterned gold. The bodies alone do not explain the difference between the images; the surfaces around them are part of the contact. These works are collection references rather than a fixed visiting route. Check the Belvedere's current display information, especially when planning around an individual painting.
